BUG REPORT (from a user of the library):
Using the random and round-robin proxy load balancers, asking for the next target when the target list is empty panics instead of returning nil. Expected: `Next` returns nil so the caller can respond with a "no target available" error.

Reproduction:
```go
rb := NewRandomBalancer(nil)
rb.Next(c) // panic: invalid argument to Intn

rrb := NewRoundRobinBalancer([]*ProxyTarget{})
rrb.Next(c) // panic: runtime error: integer divide by zero
```

Relevant code: /echo/middleware/proxy.go (randomBalancer.Next at ~line 177, roundRobinBalancer.Next at ~line 187, and the ProxyWithConfig middleware which calls config.Balancer.Next(c) at ~line 231).

WHAT TO DO:
1. First run the existing test suite to record a baseline of which tests pass/fail BEFORE any edit: `cd /echo && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -50` (also `go vet ./middleware/` if useful). Record exactly which tests fail at baseline (these are the only ones allowed to fail afterwards).
2. Fix the bug so that both balancers' `Next` return nil when there are no targets (no panic). Keep the fix minimal and idiomatic; keep thread-safety of the existing mutex usage in mind (roundRobinBalancer.Next currently does not lock at all - do not introduce a data race regression, but do not over-engineer).
3. Make sure the proxy middleware does not itself panic when the balancer returns nil (a nil target would otherwise be dereferenced in proxyHTTP/proxyRaw). Choose the minimal, sane behavior consistent with the rest of the file (e.g. returning an echo.HTTPError such as echo.ErrServiceUnavailable / http.StatusServiceUnavailable) and make sure it does not break any existing test. Note: in the middleware, `c.Set(config.ContextKey, tgt)` and the header rewriting happen before proxying; keep changes minimal.
4. Write a temporary throwaway verification (e.g. a small program under /tmp, NOT a test file inside /echo, and NOT committed) that calls both balancers' Next with an empty target list and asserts nil is returned and no panic occurs. Also verify with `go test ./middleware/ -run TestProxy -count=1` and the full `go test ./...` that nothing regressed compared to the baseline. You may add a NEW test file only if it is clearly additive (e.g. /echo/middleware/proxy_balancer_empty_test.go) - but it is safer to verify with a throwaway program in /tmp; do not modify existing test files.
5. Report back concisely: the exact diff you made (file + code), the baseline test results, the post-fix test results, and the verification output proving nil is returned with no panic. If you could not fix it, say why.

BUG REPORT (from a user of the library):
`Context.Scheme()` is used to build absolute URLs. A proxy in front of the app sometimes sends an X-Forwarded-Proto value that isn't a real scheme (e.g. "ftp"), and the user also sets X-Url-Scheme: https as a fallback. Expected: Scheme() should ignore the bogus/invalid scheme value and fall back to the next valid source (X-Url-Scheme), or default to "http" if nothing valid is present. Actual: it returns the bogus value, so generated links use ftp://.

Reproduction:
```go
c.Request().Header.Set("X-Forwarded-Proto", "ftp")
c.Request().Header.Set("X-Url-Scheme", "https")
fmt.Println(c.Scheme()) // prints "ftp", expected "https"
```

WHERE TO LOOK: /echo/context.go, method `Scheme()` (and any helpers it uses). Also read its doc comment (the in-repo contract for expected behavior), and check the constant list for header names (echo.HeaderXForwardedProto, echo.HeaderXURLScheme) in /echo/echo.go. Check whether there is an existing helper/constant listing valid schemes in the repo (grep for "https", "scheme", "X-Url-Scheme", "X-Forwarded-Proto").

WHAT TO DO:
1. FIRST run the baseline test suite and record exactly which tests pass/fail BEFORE any edit: `cd /echo && go build ./... && go test ./... -count=1 2>&1 | tail -40`. Also grep the pre-existing tests for Scheme() usage (context_test.go, echo_test.go, middleware tests) and note what they assert about X-Forwarded-Proto / X-Url-Scheme, including any test that expects a bogus value to be returned. IMPORTANT: if a pre-existing test asserts the current (buggy) behavior, do NOT modify that test; report it precisely and stop (the bug would then be out of scope).
2. Fix `Scheme()` minimally so that only valid schemes are accepted from X-Forwarded-Proto / X-Url-Scheme (and any other source it consults), falling back to the next source and finally to "http" (and "https" when the request is TLS, per the existing code). Decide the set of valid schemes from what the repository itself documents/uses (e.g. http, https, ws, wss if the repo references them) - keep it minimal and justified by in-repo evidence; explain your choice in the report. Preserve the existing precedence order of headers and the TLS behavior.
3. Verify: `go test ./... -count=1` must show the same results as the baseline (no pre-existing green test may fail). Also write a throwaway program OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/verifscheme/main.go, own module with a `replace github.com/labstack/echo/v4 => /echo` directive) that constructs an echo context with httptest and checks: X-Forwarded-Proto=ftp + X-Url-Scheme=https -> "https"; X-Forwarded-Proto=ftp only -> "http"; X-Forwarded-Proto=https -> "https"; no headers, non-TLS -> "http"; no headers, TLS -> "https"; X-Url-Scheme=ftp only -> "http". Run it with `go run -race` if feasible. Delete the throwaway program afterwards; do not add any file inside /echo.
4. Report back concisely: the exact diff (file + code), the baseline vs post-fix test results, the throwaway verification output, and anything you deliberately did not change and why.

BUG REPORT (from a user of the library):
When a request does not match any registered route, the context still reports the requested URL as its path, so you cannot tell "no route matched" apart from a real match. Expected: `c.Path()` returns "" (empty) when no route matched, because it is documented as the path of the matched route.

Reproduction:
```go
e := echo.New()
e.GET("/users/:id", handler)
e.HTTPErrorHandler = func(err error, c echo.Context) {
    fmt.Println(c.Path()) // requesting /does-not-exist prints "/does-not-exist", expected ""
}
```
Only unmatched requests show this; matched requests behave as documented.

WHERE TO LOOK: /echo/echo.go (ServeHTTP, where the router is invoked and where `c.path` / `c.SetPath(...)` is assigned on the not-found path), /echo/context.go (`Path()`/`SetPath()` and the `path` field), and /echo/router.go. Check the doc comments of `Context.Path()` and `Echo.ServeHTTP`/router behavior to confirm the expected contract.

WHAT TO DO:
1. FIRST run the baseline test suite and record exactly which tests pass/fail BEFORE any edit: `cd /echo && go build ./... && go test ./... -count=1 2>&1 | tail -40`. Also check whether any pre-existing test asserts the current (buggy) behavior of `c.Path()` for unmatched routes - grep the test files for `Path()` and for not-found / 404 handling (e.g. in echo_test.go, context_test.go, router_test.go). IMPORTANT: if a pre-existing test asserts the buggy behavior, do NOT change that test; instead report it and stop (that bug would then be out of scope).
2. Fix the bug minimally so that `c.Path()` returns "" when no route matched, while matched routes keep returning the route path (including the router's path with params, e.g. "/users/:id"). Be careful: `c.SetPath()` may also be used by middleware and by the proxy/rewrite logic; do not break those. Also check whether other code depends on `c.path` being set for unmatched requests (e.g. error handling, `c.Path()` usage in middleware such as the logger, request_id, or the `Echo#ServeHTTP` code that handles `MethodNotAllowed`/`NotFound`).
3. Verify: `go test ./... -count=1` must show the same results as the baseline (no pre-existing green test may fail). Additionally write a throwaway program OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/verifypath/main.go, its own module with a `replace` directive pointing at /echo, or use `go run` with the repo's module) that starts an echo server with an HTTPErrorHandler printing `c.Path()` and confirms: matched route -> route path (e.g. "/users/:id"), unmatched route -> "". Run it with `go run -race` if feasible. Delete the throwaway program afterwards; do not add any file inside /echo.
4. Report back concisely: the exact diff (file + code), the baseline vs post-fix test results, the throwaway verification output, and anything you deliberately did not change and why.

BUG REPORT (from a user of the library):
Binding query parameters into a map does not work as expected when a key appears more than once.
- With a `map[string][]string` destination, `c.Bind(&m)` panics with a message like `reflect: SetMapIndex: value of type string is not assignable to type []string` instead of collecting all values per key.
- With a `map[string]interface{}` destination it does not panic, but each key ends up holding a single string instead of the slice of values.

Reproduction:
```go
m := map[string][]string{}
if err := c.Bind(&m); err != nil { return err }
```
For a request like `?tag=a&tag=b` the user expects `m` to be `{"tag": ["a", "b"]}`.

WHERE TO LOOK: /echo/bind.go (the `bindData` / `bindDataToMap`-style code that handles map destinations, and `setWithProperType`), and /echo/binder.go (the newer Binder implementation, `bindData`/`bindMap`-ish paths) - check which one `c.Bind`/`DefaultBinder` actually uses in this revision, and read the doc comments of `Bind`, `BindQueryParams`, and any in-repo documentation/README/CHANGELOG statements about binding into maps to establish the expected contract. Also check the existing tests (bind_test.go, binder_test.go) for map binding expectations.

WHAT TO DO:
1. FIRST run the baseline test suite and record exactly which tests pass/fail BEFORE any edit: `cd /echo && go build ./... && go test ./... -count=1 2>&1 | tail -40`. Grep the pre-existing tests for map binding cases (e.g. `map[string]interface{}`, `map[string][]string`, `Bind` into maps) and note exactly what they assert. IMPORTANT: if a pre-existing test asserts the current (buggy) behavior (e.g. expects a single string for a repeated key, or expects the panic), do NOT modify that test; report it precisely and stop (that part of the bug would then be out of scope).
2. Fix the bug minimally so that binding into a map collects all values for repeated keys: `map[string][]string` must not panic and must be `{"tag": ["a", "b"]}` for `?tag=a&tag=b`; `map[string]interface{}` should hold the slice of values for repeated keys (and keep a single string for single-valued keys if that is what the existing tests require - check carefully and keep any behavior that pre-existing green tests depend on). Keep the change minimal and idiomatic, and do not break binding into structs, slices, or other map value types.
3. Verify: `go test ./... -count=1` must show the same results as the baseline (no pre-existing green test may fail). Also write a throwaway program OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/verifmap/main.go, own module with a `replace github.com/labstack/echo/v4 => /echo` directive) that exercises: `?tag=a&tag=b` into map[string][]string, into map[string]interface{}, `?a=1` into map[string]string, `?a=1` into map[string]int, plus a form POST body and a JSON body into a map, and confirm no panic and the expected contents. Run with `go run -race` if feasible. Delete the throwaway program afterwards; do not add any file inside /echo.
4. Report back concisely: the exact diff (file + code), the baseline vs post-fix test results, the throwaway verification output, and anything you deliberately did not change and why.

BUG REPORT (from a user of the library):
Registering two route groups that share the same path prefix, each with its own middleware, breaks the routes of the first group.

Reproduction:
```go
e := echo.New()
g1 := e.Group("/group", m1)
g1.GET("", h)
g2 := e.Group("/group", m2)
g2.GET("/other", h)
```
Expected: `GET /group` runs `h` with `m1`, and `GET /group/other` runs `h` with `m2`. Actual: `GET /group` returns 404 Not Found even though it was registered; only the second group's route works. Deleting the second group makes the first one work again.

WHERE TO LOOK: /echo/group.go (`Group`, `Add`, `GET`, and how the group prefix is joined with the route path, e.g. `g.prefix + path`), and /echo/echo.go (`Echo.add`, `Echo.Add`, and the router registration). Pay attention to how the path is normalized when the group prefix is used and the route path is empty ("") - a trailing-slash/empty-path normalization bug is the likely cause (e.g. registering "/group/" instead of "/group", or the router's trailing-slash redirect interacting with it). Also check /echo/router.go for how a registered path is stored/looked up, and /echo/middleware/slash.go behavior. Read the doc comments of `Group` and `Add` for the in-repo contract.

WHAT TO DO:
1. FIRST run the baseline test suite and record exactly which tests pass/fail BEFORE any edit: `cd /echo && go build ./... && go test ./... -count=1 2>&1 | tail -40`. Grep the pre-existing tests for group tests with empty route paths and same-prefix groups (group_test.go, echo_test.go, router_test.go) and note what they assert. IMPORTANT: if a pre-existing test asserts the current (buggy) behavior, do NOT modify that test; report it precisely and stop (the bug would then be out of scope).
2. Fix the bug minimally so that both groups' routes work as expected: `GET /group` reaches the handler registered with `g1.GET("", h)` (with m1 applied) and `GET /group/other` reaches g2's route with m2 applied. Do not break other group/route registration behavior (nested groups, prefixes with/without trailing slash, `Group.Add`, `Echo.Add`, `Any`, route params).
3. Verify: `go test ./... -count=1` must show the same results as the baseline (no pre-existing green test may fail). Also write a throwaway program OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/verifgroup/main.go, own module with a `replace github.com/labstack/echo/v4 => /echo` directive) that reproduces the user's exact scenario with two groups sharing the prefix, asserts GET /group runs h with m1 and GET /group/other runs h with m2, plus a few related cases (group with trailing-slash prefix, nested groups, a group route with a param). Run it with `go run -race` if feasible. Delete the throwaway program afterwards; do not add any file inside /echo.
4. Report back concisely: the exact diff (file + code), the baseline vs post-fix test results, the throwaway verification output, and anything you deliberately did not change and why.

BUG REPORT (from a user of the library):
With the gzip compression middleware enabled and a client sending `Accept-Encoding: gzip`, a handler that returns an empty string with status 200 produces an invalid response: the body is gzip data (starts with the gzip magic bytes) but the `Content-Encoding: gzip` header is missing, so HTTP clients see garbage / fail to parse it as text. Expected: either a valid gzip stream WITH `Content-Encoding: gzip` (and `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8`), or an uncompressed empty body.

Reproduction:
```go
e := echo.New()
e.Use(middleware.Gzip())
e.GET("/empty", func(c echo.Context) error { return c.String(http.StatusOK, "") })
```
Request with `Accept-Encoding: gzip`; observe the response body/headers.

WHERE TO LOOK: /echo/middleware/compress.go (the gzip ResponseWriter wrapper, how it decides to write the gzip header, when it sets the `Content-Encoding` header, and how it handles zero-length bodies / `WriteHeader` / `Close`), and /echo/response.go (`Response.WriteHeader`, `Response.Write`, and any `beforeFuncs` / `Content-Length` handling) since the interaction between the wrapper and the response writer is likely the cause. Read the doc comments of `Gzip`/`GzipWithConfig` for the in-repo contract.

WHAT TO DO:
1. FIRST run the baseline test suite and record exactly which tests pass/fail BEFORE any edit: `cd /echo && go build ./... && go test ./... -count=1 2>&1 | tail -40`. Grep the pre-existing tests (middleware/compress_test.go, response_test.go, middleware/decompress_test.go) for empty-body / zero-length cases and note exactly what they assert. IMPORTANT: if a pre-existing test asserts the current (buggy) behavior, do NOT modify that test; report it precisely and stop (the bug would then be out of scope).
2. Fix the bug minimally so the response is consistent: the gzip stream and the `Content-Encoding` header must agree. The preferred minimal fix is that when the body is empty the middleware does not emit a gzip body at all (no gzip magic bytes) OR emits a complete valid gzip stream together with `Content-Encoding: gzip`; pick whichever is the smaller change that keeps all existing tests green and does not break the existing non-empty compression behavior, the `Content-Length`/`Content-Type` handling, or the other compressors (deflate/br) if they share the code path. Explain your choice.
3. Verify: `go test ./... -count=1` must show the same results as the baseline (no pre-existing green test may fail). Also write a throwaway program OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/verifgzip/main.go, own module with a `replace github.com/labstack/echo/v4 => /echo` directive) that uses httptest to check: (a) empty string body with Accept-Encoding: gzip -> either no gzip magic bytes and no Content-Encoding, or valid gzip stream + Content-Encoding: gzip, and in the gzip case that `gzip.NewReader` can decompress it to ""; (b) non-empty body -> still compressed and decompressible to the original; (c) 204/304 status responses and a HEAD request behave sanely; (d) a handler that writes nothing at all. Run it with `go run -race` if feasible. Delete the throwaway program afterwards; do not add any file inside /echo.
4. Report back concisely: the exact diff (file + code), the baseline vs post-fix test results, the throwaway verification output, and anything you deliberately did not change and why.
